examples.english: To go through the baptism of the real world.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新人|しんじん}→新人：02500_shinjin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧{洗礼|せんれい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}けた→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧。

examples.english: On my first day of the overseas posting, I was baptized by the reality of cultural differences.

notes:
Originally a Christian religious term for the sacrament of baptism. In Japanese, the figurative sense of a harsh or transformative first experience is used much more commonly than the religious sense.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {洗礼|せんれい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧: to receive baptism; to undergo an initiation
- {洗礼|せんれい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{浴|あ}びる→浴びる：02844_abiru⟧: to be hit with an ordeal (figurative)
- {洗礼|せんれい}{名|めい}: baptismal name
- {洗礼式|せんれいしき}: baptism ceremony
- ⟦{社会|しゃかい}→社会：01427_shakai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{洗礼|せんれい}: the baptism of the real world

USAGE:
The figurative sense 2 is far more common in everyday Japanese. It typically describes a newcomer's difficult first encounter with something — a new job, a new environment, or harsh reality. The phrase {洗礼|せんれい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧ works for both senses.
